termDefinitions.meaning: 用一把锁保护一整个对象的全部状态，简单但会串行化无关的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A coarse-grained lock guards an entire object's state with one lock: simple, but it serializes unrelated operations.

scenario: Warehouse.removeStock 没有加锁，阈值是 10，两个线程几乎同时把库存从 12 各扣掉 2。
scenario_en: Warehouse.removeStock has no lock, the threshold is 10, and two threads each remove 2 units from a stock of 12 at almost the same moment.
q: 除了丢更新，无锁还会造成什么？
q_en: Beyond lost updates, what else does the missing lock cause?
options: 两个线程读到同样的旧数量，都判定为下穿阈值并各报一次警
告警会因为数量对不上而被两个线程都跳过，一次都不发
阈值穿越判断本身是纯计算，不受并发影响，只有数量会算错
两个线程会各自把 alertConfigs 里的配置删掉一份，之后再也不报警
options_en: Both threads read the same stale quantity, both see a downward crossing, and both fire an alert.
Both threads skip the alert because the quantities disagree, so none is ever sent.
The crossing check is pure computation and immune to concurrency; only the quantity ends up wrong.
Each thread deletes one entry from alertConfigs, so no alert ever fires again.
optionExplanations: 两边的 previousQty 都读成 12、newQty 都算成 10 以下，条件同时成立。
条件是同时成立而不是同时不成立，这个方向正好想反了。
计算是纯的，但输入的 previousQty 来自共享 map，读到陈旧值就会算错。
getAlertsToFire 只读配置列表，不会删除任何 AlertConfig。
optionExplanations_en: Both sides read previousQty as 12 and compute newQty below 10, so the crossing condition holds twice.
The condition holds on both sides rather than failing on both — this has the direction backwards.
The computation is pure, but previousQty comes from the shared map, so a stale read makes it wrong.
getAlertsToFire only reads the config list; it never removes an AlertConfig.
why: 无锁的 read-modify-write 让两个线程拿到同一份陈旧 previousQty，穿越条件被重复判真。加锁后阈值穿越的去重语义才成立。
why_en: Without a lock the read-modify-write lets both threads see the same stale previousQty, so the crossing check fires twice — the dedup semantics only hold under the lock.
tradeoff: 无锁吞吐 vs 库存数量与告警去重的正确性
whenOtherWins: 如果每个产品的写入天然只由一个线程负责，就不存在陈旧读，这把锁可以省掉。

termDefinitions.meaning: 先读出当前值、算出新值、再写回去的三步操作，不加锁就会互相覆盖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read-modify-write reads a value, computes a new one and writes it back; without a lock two threads clobber each other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读到的是别的线程已经改过、但本线程还没看到的旧值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stale read returns an old value that another thread has already changed but this thread hasn't seen.

scenario: getAlertsToFire 是 Warehouse 的私有方法，只被已处于 synchronized(this) 内的 addStock 和 removeStock 调用。
scenario_en: getAlertsToFire is a private Warehouse method, called only from addStock and removeStock while they already hold synchronized(this).
q: 它自己还要不要再加一层同步？
q_en: Should it add its own layer of synchronization?
options: 不用，调用方已持锁，再加同步在非重入锁下反而会自锁
要，凡是读共享 map 的方法都必须自己加同步才安全
要，因为它会调用 listener，回调必须被锁保护起来
不用，因为它读到的 alertConfigs 是一份线程私有的拷贝
options_en: No — the caller already holds the lock, and re-locking would self-deadlock under a non-reentrant lock.
Yes — any method that reads a shared map must synchronize itself to be safe.
Yes — it invokes the listener, and that callback has to be protected by the lock.
No — the alertConfigs it reads is a thread-private copy.
optionExplanations: 锁已经在外层拿到，重复加锁没有新收益，还得依赖锁的可重入性。
私有方法不是入口，它的安全由唯一的调用路径保证而不是自己声明。
它只收集待触发的 listener，真正的回调在释放锁之后才执行。
它直接读的就是共享的 alertConfigs，并没有做任何拷贝。
optionExplanations_en: The lock is already held one frame up, so re-acquiring adds nothing and leans on reentrancy.
A private method is not an entry point; its safety comes from its single call path, not its own declaration.
It only collects the listeners to fire — the actual callback runs after the lock is released.
It reads the shared alertConfigs directly; no copy is made anywhere.
why: 私有方法的线程安全由调用约定保证：调用方全程持锁。代价是这条约定必须写清楚，否则以后有人从锁外调用它就破防。
why_en: The private method's thread safety rests on a calling convention — every caller holds the lock — so that convention has to be documented or a future caller breaks it.
tradeoff: 靠调用约定省一层锁 vs 方法自带同步更防呆
whenOtherWins: 如果这个方法以后要暴露成 public 供外部直接调用，它就必须自己加同步。

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一个线程可以重复获取自己已经持有的锁而不会卡死，如 Java 的 synchronized。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reentrant lock lets the same thread acquire a lock it already holds without deadlocking, like Java's synchronized.

scenario: 为提高吞吐改成 per-product 锁，让不同产品真正并行，但 inventory 仍然是普通 HashMap。
scenario_en: To raise throughput you switch to per-product locks so different products truly run in parallel, but inventory is still a plain HashMap.
q: 为什么这时必须换成 ConcurrentHashMap？
q_en: Why must the map become a ConcurrentHashMap at this point?
options: 即使操作不同 key，HashMap 的扩容和桶管理也会被并发破坏
因为普通 HashMap 不支持用字符串 productId 当键
HashMap 在不同 key 上本来就是安全的，只是速度会慢一些
因为 ConcurrentHashMap 会自动按 productId 帮你加好每个产品的锁
options_en: Even for different keys, a HashMap's resizing and bucket bookkeeping get corrupted under concurrency.
A plain HashMap doesn't support string productIds as keys.
A HashMap is already safe across different keys; it's just somewhat slower.
ConcurrentHashMap automatically takes a per-product lock keyed by productId for you.
optionExplanations: resize 时数组和链表被同时改写，可能丢条目甚至读到损坏的结构。
键类型跟线程安全无关，HashMap 一直支持字符串键。
不同 key 落进同一个桶或同时触发 resize 就会互相踩，这个前提不成立。
它保护的是 map 结构本身，read-modify-write 仍要靠你自己的 productLocks。
optionExplanations_en: During a resize the array and its chains are rewritten concurrently, dropping entries or corrupting structure.
Key type has nothing to do with thread safety; HashMap has always accepted string keys.
Different keys can land in the same bucket or trigger a resize together, so that premise is false.
It protects the map structure itself; your read-modify-write still needs your own productLocks.
why: per-product 锁只保护单个产品的读改写，map 结构本身的并发修改要靠线程安全容器。代价是多一层容器开销和更难推理的边界。
why_en: Per-product locks only guard one product's read-modify-write, so the map structure itself needs a thread-safe container underneath.
tradeoff: 细粒度锁提高并发 vs 需要线程安全容器兜底结构安全
whenOtherWins: 仓库级单锁下所有访问本来就串行，普通 HashMap 完全够用，不必换容器。

termDefinitions.meaning: 线程安全的哈希表，内部保护自己的桶和扩容，多个线程可同时读写不同键。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ConcurrentHashMap is a thread-safe hash table that guards its own buckets and resizing so threads can touch different keys at once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 哈希表元素变多时重新分配更大的数组并把所有条目搬过去。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Resizing allocates a larger array when a hash table grows and rehashes every entry into it.

scenario: per-product 锁存在 productLocks 这张 map 里，仓库上线几年会见过上百万个不同的 productId。
scenario_en: The per-product locks live in a productLocks map, and over a few years the warehouse will have seen millions of distinct productIds.
q: 这些锁对象该何时创建、何时删除？
q_en: When should a per-product lock object be created, and when removed?
options: 第一次见到该产品时创建，之后基本不回收，内存代价可接受
每次操作结束就把这把锁从 map 里删掉，避免内存增长
系统启动时按产品目录一次性把所有锁全部预先创建好
给每把锁配一个定时器，闲置超过一分钟就自动销毁并重建
options_en: Create one the first time you see the product and basically never reclaim it; the memory cost is fine.
Delete the lock from the map as soon as each operation finishes, to avoid unbounded growth.
Pre-create every lock at startup by walking the product catalog.
Give each lock a timer that destroys and recreates it after a minute of being idle.
optionExplanations: 一个锁对象只有几十字节，百万级产品也就几十 MB，换来的是不用做回收。
删除的瞬间可能有线程正要拿这把锁，随后两边会锁到不同对象上。
产品目录在本系统之外，服务只在收到 productId 时才知道它存在。
定时销毁把删除竞态变成周期性发生，问题更难复现也更难排查。
optionExplanations_en: A lock object is a few dozen bytes, so even millions of products cost tens of megabytes and no reclamation logic.
At the instant you delete it another thread may be about to acquire it, and the two then lock different objects.
The product catalog lives outside this system; the service learns a productId exists only when it arrives.
A timer turns the deletion race into a recurring event, making the bug harder to reproduce.
why: 安全回收锁很难，因为无法确定没有线程正要获取它；按需创建、只增不减是标准做法。代价是 productLocks 随见过的产品数单调增长。
why_en: Reclaiming a lock safely is hard because you can't prove no thread is about to grab it, so you create on first use and never remove.
tradeoff: 只增不减避开回收竞态 vs map 长期占用内存
whenOtherWins: 如果 productId 是一次性生成的（比如按批次），锁 map 会无界增长，就得做带引用计数的回收。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一把大锁拆成按 key 分配的多把小锁，让不同 key 的操作并行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lock striping splits one big lock into many keyed locks so operations on different keys can run in parallel.

scenario: 结账占了 5 分钟的 reservation，清理任务每分钟扫一次过期占用，此刻支付回调才到达并调用 confirmReservation。
scenario_en: A checkout held a 5-minute reservation, a cleanup task sweeps expired ones every minute, and the payment callback only now calls confirmReservation.
q: confirmReservation 必须先做哪一步校验？
q_en: What must confirmReservation validate first?
options: 比较当前时间和 reservation.expiresAt，已过期就返回 false
确认 reserved[productId] 大于等于本次要确认的数量
检查这个 productId 上还有没有别的 reservation 正在排队等待
重新调用一次 checkAvailability，确认可售库存仍然够本次订单
options_en: Compare the current time with reservation.expiresAt and return false if it has expired.
Confirm that reserved[productId] is at least the quantity being confirmed.
Check whether any other reservation for this productId is still queued behind it.
Call checkAvailability again to confirm the sellable stock still covers this order.
optionExplanations: 过期的占用可能已被清理任务释放并卖给别人，直接扣减就会超卖。
这个计数在 reserve 和 release 里各自增减，不是确认时的判据。
别人的占用早就从可售数量里扣掉了，不影响本次能否确认。
预占的意义正是不必重查可售量，重查等于把 reservation 白做了。
optionExplanations_en: An expired hold may already have been released by the cleanup task and sold to someone else.
That counter is incremented on reserve and decremented on release; it isn't the check that matters at confirm time.
Other people's holds were already subtracted from the sellable pool, so they don't gate this confirm.
The whole point of reserving is not having to re-check availability; re-checking wastes the reservation.
why: reservation 是一份有到期时间的库存租约，过期后那批数量可能已被清理任务释放给别人。代价是卡在边界的合法支付会被拒。
why_en: A reservation is a lease with an expiry, and once it lapses the cleanup task may have already handed those units to someone else.
tradeoff: 严格校验过期防超卖 vs 放宽校验保住已付款订单
whenOtherWins: 如果没有清理任务、占用只能显式释放，过期时间就只是提示，可以不做这次校验。

termDefinitions.meaning: 创建 reservation 时算出的 currentTime + timeoutMs，超过它这份占用即失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: expiresAt is currentTime plus the timeout, computed when the reservation is created; past it, the hold is void.

termDefinitions.meaning: 周期性扫描 reservations、把已过期的调用 releaseReservation 放回可售池的后台线程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The cleanup task is a background loop that scans reservations and releases the expired ones back into the sellable pool.

scenario: reservation 超时设为 5 分钟，一笔订单在第 5 分 10 秒回调成功，而支付其实早在窗口内就已发起。
scenario_en: The reservation timeout is 5 minutes and an order's callback lands at 5 minutes 10 seconds, though the payment itself began inside the window.
q: 该不该给这类刚过期的占用一个宽限期？
q_en: Should a just-expired reservation get a grace period?
options: 该给：支付已在进行中，硬拒会白白丢掉一笔已收的钱
不该给：任何宽限都会让超时时间失去意义，必须一刀切
该给：把超时时间直接改成一小时，宽限期就不需要了
不该给：应当把清理任务改成每毫秒扫描一次，杜绝边界情况
options_en: Yes — payment is already in flight, and a hard rejection throws away money you've collected.
No — any grace period makes the timeout meaningless, so the cutoff must be absolute.
Yes — just raise the timeout to an hour and you won't need a grace period at all.
No — sweep for expired reservations every millisecond instead and the edge case disappears.
optionExplanations: 边界上的损失是真金白银，多放行几秒的超卖概率远小于丢单成本。
超时是为了释放僵尸占用，不是为了惩罚正在付款的用户。
一小时会让热门商品长时间不可售，等于把不可卖窗口放大十几倍。
扫描再密也消不掉边界，只会让清理任务自己长期占着仓库锁。
optionExplanations_en: The loss at the boundary is real revenue, and a few extra seconds of oversell risk costs far less.
The timeout exists to free zombie holds, not to punish a customer who is mid-payment.
An hour keeps hot items unsellable far longer, stretching the blocked window more than tenfold.
No sweep frequency removes the boundary; it just keeps the cleanup task holding the warehouse lock.
why: 超时长度和宽限期都是商业决策：一头是被抢走占用的用户，一头是没抢到货的用户。代价是宽限窗口内确认的订单有小概率真超卖。
why_en: Both the timeout and the grace period are business calls, balancing the customer who loses a hold against the customer who never got stock.
tradeoff: 严格超时保公平 vs 宽限期保成交
whenOtherWins: 限量发售这类强调公平的场景，宁可拒掉迟到的确认，也不让超时的人插队。

termDefinitions.meaning: 超时之后再留一小段时间，允许支付已在进行中的 reservation 仍被确认。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A grace period is a short window after expiry during which a reservation whose payment is already in flight can still be confirmed.

scenario: 库存已从源仓扣出、交给 Transfer 对象持有，卡车在路上要跑 3-5 天。
scenario_en: The stock has left the source warehouse and is held by a Transfer object while the truck spends three to five days on the road.
q: 到货和运输取消这两条路径分别怎么收尾？
q_en: How do the arrival path and the cancellation path each finish?
options: 到货把数量加到目标仓并删除 Transfer；取消则把数量退回源仓
到货把数量加到目标仓，取消时直接丢弃这条 Transfer 记录
到货和取消都只改 Transfer 的状态字段，库存就留在 Transfer 里不动
在途期间目标仓就已计入这批库存，收尾只需要删掉 Transfer 记录
options_en: Arrival credits the destination and deletes the Transfer; cancellation returns the units to the source.
Arrival credits the destination, and cancellation simply discards the Transfer record.
Both paths just flip a status field on the Transfer and the stock stays inside it.
The destination already counts the units while in transit, so finishing just deletes the Transfer.
optionExplanations: 两条路径都让这批数量回到某个 Warehouse，系统总量始终守恒。
丢弃记录等于把货物凭空销账，取消一次就少一批库存。
库存永远停在 Transfer 里，目标仓拿不到货，可售量再也不恢复。
在途期间两边都不该可售，提前计入会让目标仓卖出还没到的货。
optionExplanations_en: Both paths land the units back in some Warehouse, so the system total stays conserved.
Discarding the record writes the goods off into nothing; one cancellation silently destroys stock.
The units stay parked in the Transfer forever, so the destination never receives them.
Neither side should count in-transit units as sellable, or the destination sells goods that haven't arrived.
why: Transfer 是临时持有者：completeTransfer 把数量交给目标仓后删除记录，取消则把数量退回源仓。代价是多一个实体和它的清理逻辑。
why_en: The Transfer is a temporary holder: completing it hands the units to the destination and drops the record, while cancelling returns them to the source.
tradeoff: 在途实体让总量随时可核对 vs 瞬移模型代码更少
whenOtherWins: 如果调拨是同一栋楼内几分钟完成，双锁瞬移模型足够，不必引入 Transfer 实体。

termDefinitions.meaning: Warehouse 和 Transfer 共同实现的接口，表示任何可以持有库存的地方。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: InventoryHolder is the interface shared by Warehouse and Transfer, representing anywhere stock can live.

termDefinitions.meaning: 已离开源仓、尚未到达目标仓的那批数量，不可售但仍计入系统总量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In-transit inventory has left the source but not yet arrived: not sellable, but still counted in the system total.

scenario: 调用方传入一个不存在的 warehouseId，分别调用 InventoryManager.addStock 和 removeStock。
scenario_en: A caller passes a nonexistent warehouseId to InventoryManager.addStock and to removeStock.
q: 这两个方法对无效 warehouseId 的处理方式一致吗？
q_en: Do these two methods handle an invalid warehouseId the same way?
options: 不一致：addStock 抛错，removeStock 返回 false
一致：两者遇到无效仓库都抛出同一异常
一致：两者都静默跳过，不返回任何错误信号
不一致：removeStock 抛错，addStock 返回 false
options_en: Inconsistent: addStock throws, while removeStock just returns false.
Consistent: both throw the same exception for a missing warehouse.
Consistent: both silently skip, with no error signal at all.
Inconsistent: removeStock throws, and addStock returns false.
optionExplanations: 调用方要为同一个根因写两套判断：一处 catch 异常，一处检查布尔值。
两者走的是不同分支，一个 throw 一个 return false，并非同一种异常。
addStock 找不到仓库会直接抛错中断调用，并不是被静默跳过。
方向说反了：源码里 throw 的是 addStock，return false 的是 removeStock。
optionExplanations_en: A caller ends up writing two different checks for the same root cause: catch an exception here, check a boolean there.
They take different branches — one throws, one returns false — not the same exception.
addStock throws and stops the call outright; it isn't silently skipped.
This reverses it: the code throws in addStock and returns false in removeStock.
why: addStock 对无效 warehouseId 直接 throw，removeStock 却和库存不足一样返回 false，两种失败信号并不对称。
why_en: addStock throws on an invalid warehouseId, while removeStock returns false just like it does for insufficient stock — the two failure signals aren't symmetric.
tradeoff: throw 让调用方无法忽略错误 vs return false 能把所有失败原因合并成一次判断
whenOtherWins: 如果团队约定所有失败都用返回值表达，应把 addStock 也改成返回 boolean，保持两者一致。

scenario: 团队要在 naive、defensive、atomic 三版 transfer 里选一个上生产。
scenario_en: The team must pick one of the naive, defensive, and atomic transfer versions for production.
q: 哪一版必须排除，另外两版又是什么取舍？
q_en: Which version must be excluded, and what tradeoff separates the other two?
options: naive 排除（正确性 bug）；defensive、atomic 都可接受
naive 和 defensive 都必须排除，只有 atomic 版本能被允许上生产
三版性能有差异但逻辑都正确，选哪个纯粹看团队喜好
atomic 必须排除，因为它会同时锁住两个仓库拖累吞吐
options_en: naive is out (a correctness bug); defensive and atomic are both acceptable.
Both naive and defensive must be excluded; only the atomic version is allowed in production.
All three are logically correct with only performance differences; pick by team taste.
atomic must be excluded because locking two warehouses at once drags down throughput.
optionExplanations: 只有一版有真正的正确性缺陷，另外两版只是并发度和一致性程度之间的选择。
defensive 已经用 removeStock 返回值堵住了 TOCTOU，没有正确性 bug，不必一并排除。
naive 那版会真的丢库存或产生幻影库存，不是三版都正确、只看喜好。
锁两个仓库换来的是外部可观察的真原子性，是可接受的代价，不是必须排除的缺陷。
optionExplanations_en: Only one version has a genuine correctness defect; the other two are a choice between concurrency and consistency level.
defensive already closes the TOCTOU race via removeStock's return value, so it has no correctness bug to exclude.
naive genuinely loses or duplicates stock — it isn't a case of all three being correct.
Locking two warehouses buys externally visible true atomicity, an acceptable cost, not a defect to rule out.
why: naive 是正确性 bug（幻影库存），生产不可接受；defensive 和 atomic 都正确，只在中间态可见性和并发度间取舍。
why_en: naive has a real correctness bug and is never production-acceptable; defensive and atomic are both correct, differing only in intermediate-state visibility and concurrency cost.
tradeoff: defensive 并发更高、允许短暂中间态 vs atomic 强一致但锁两仓库
whenOtherWins: 只要没人做跨仓总量聚合查询，defensive 换来的并发提升通常更划算。

scenario: 结账 reservation 超时可以设 30 秒，也可以设 10 分钟。
scenario_en: The checkout reservation timeout could be set to 30 seconds or to 10 minutes.
q: 该怎么在这两个极端之间选超时长度？
q_en: How should the timeout length be chosen between these two extremes?
options: 太短挤掉正在填单的用户，太长占用库存，多数落在 5-15 分钟
只要系统吞吐扛得住，超时长短对用户体验来说完全没有任何影响
越短越好，能让库存最快归还给下一个排队买家
越长越好，能保证每个点击购买的用户都能付完款
options_en: Too short cancels users mid-checkout, too long locks stock — most settle around 5-15 minutes.
As long as throughput holds up, the timeout length has zero effect on user experience.
Shorter is always better since it returns stock to the next buyer in line fastest.
Longer is always better since it guarantees every buyer who clicks can finish paying.
optionExplanations: 30 秒可能挤掉正在填支付信息的用户，10 分钟又让别人白等库存；多数电商落在 5-15 分钟。
超时太短会把还在操作的正常用户挤出结账流程，这是体验问题，不只是吞吐问题。
一味求短会误伤正在正常结账的用户，不是归还越快就一定更好。
一味求长会让热门商品长时间显示缺货，伤的是没抢到占用的那批用户。
optionExplanations_en: 30 seconds may bump users still typing payment info; 10 minutes leaves others waiting on stock — most sites land on 5-15 minutes.
A too-short timeout ejects normal users mid-checkout — a UX problem, not just a throughput one.
Chasing the shortest timeout punishes users who are checking out normally.
Chasing the longest timeout keeps hot items looking out of stock for longer, hurting everyone else.
why: 超时太短误伤正在结账的用户，太长让库存被无意义占用；这是业务权衡，多数电商落在 5-15 分钟。
why_en: Too short cancels legitimate in-progress checkouts; too long locks stock pointlessly — a business tradeoff most sites settle around 5-15 minutes.
tradeoff: 短超时保周转 vs 长超时保正常结账体验
whenOtherWins: 如果结账本身很快（一键支付），可以用更短的超时而不误伤用户。

scenario: 库存服务目录有 2000 万个 SKU，每个 SKU 一把 per-product 锁，单把锁对象约 48 字节。
scenario_en: The catalog has 20 million SKUs, one per-product lock each, and each lock object is about 48 bytes.
q: 全量锁大约占多少内存，这个数字用来判断什么？
q_en: Roughly how much memory do all the locks cost, and what does that number decide?
options: 约 2000 万×48B≈960MB，远小于服务器内存，代价可接受
约 2000 万×48B≈960GB，超过单机内存，per-product 锁不可行
锁对象大小取决于线程数，跟 SKU 数量无关，这个乘法算不出有意义的数字
只要用了 ConcurrentHashMap，内存占用就是常数，不随 SKU 数增长
options_en: About 20M × 48B ≈ 960MB, a small slice of server RAM — the cost is acceptable.
About 20M × 48B ≈ 960GB, more than a single machine has — per-product locking is infeasible.
Lock size depends on thread count, not SKU count, so this multiplication is meaningless.
Once you use ConcurrentHashMap, memory use becomes constant regardless of SKU count.
optionExplanations: 2000万×48字节≈9.6亿字节≈960MB，对比几十上百 GB 的服务器内存只占一小部分。
把字节数错当成了千倍单位，2000万×48B 算不到 GB 级别，数量级本身算错了。
锁数组大小随 key（productId）数量线性增长，跟并发线程数是两回事。
ConcurrentHashMap 管的是桶结构效率，每多存一把锁对象内存依然线性增长。
optionExplanations_en: 20M × 48 bytes ≈ 960 million bytes ≈ 960MB, a small fraction of the tens-to-hundreds of GB a server typically has.
This mistakes the unit by a thousandfold; 20M × 48B never reaches GB scale — the order of magnitude is simply wrong.
The lock array grows linearly with the number of keys (productId), which is unrelated to thread count.
ConcurrentHashMap manages bucket efficiency; storing one more lock object still costs memory linearly.
why: 总内存=SKU数×单锁字节数，2000万×48B≈960MB；这个数字用来判断 per-product 锁是否内存安全，结果是安全。
why_en: Formula: total memory = SKU count × bytes per lock, 20M × 48B ≈ 960MB — the number that answers whether per-product locking is memory-safe here, and it is.

termDefinitions.meaning: 能唯一标识一种可售商品规格的库存编码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) is a code that uniquely identifies one sellable product variant.

tradeoff: per-product 锁换来跨产品并发 vs 锁对象本身也要占内存

scenario: 面试里把 AlertListener 写成一个显式 interface；换成要上线的 JS/Python 代码。
scenario_en: The interview models AlertListener as an explicit interface; imagine this were production JS/Python code.
q: 生产代码通常会怎么表达同样的通知回调？
q_en: How would production code typically express the same notification callback?
options: 直接传函数回调，跳过专门声明接口
同样必须先定义接口类型，这门语言不支持把函数当参数传递
把回调换成同步阻塞调用，不再需要接口或函数
取消通知机制，让调用方自己轮询库存
options_en: Pass a plain function callback directly, skipping a dedicated interface.
Still must define an interface first — this language can't pass a function as a parameter.
Replace the callback with a synchronous blocking call, dropping both interface and function.
Drop notifications entirely and have the caller poll inventory instead.
optionExplanations: JS 用函数回调，Python 用 lambda，Go 用函数类型；生产代码通常直接传函数即可。
现代语言普遍把函数当一等公民，能直接传函数引用，不需要先声明接口。
换成阻塞调用没有回避通知这件事，也丢了非阻塞回调的初衷，答非所问。
轮询会让调用方持续发起无意义查询，没有解决通知问题。
optionExplanations_en: JS uses function callbacks, Python uses lambdas, Go uses function types — production code usually just passes a function.
Modern languages treat functions as first-class values and can pass a reference directly without declaring an interface.
Switching to a blocking call doesn't avoid notification and loses the point of a non-blocking callback — off target.
Polling makes the caller fire pointless repeated queries and never actually solves notification.
why: interface 在面试里更明确、跨语言通用；生产 JS/Python/Go 代码通常直接传函数回调，效果等价但样板代码更少。
why_en: An interface is clearer and language-agnostic for interview explanation, but production JS/Python/Go code usually just passes a function callback with less boilerplate for the same effect.
tradeoff: interface 显式结构 vs 函数回调更少样板代码
whenOtherWins: 如果通知逻辑本身有多个方法或要携带状态，interface/class 仍然比单个函数更合适。

q: 按顺序排列 confirmReservation 成功路径的三步操作：
q_en: Put the three mutations of a successful confirmReservation in order:
steps: 从 inventory[productId] 里真正扣减这笔数量
从 reserved[productId] 里减去同样的数量，释放占用
把这条 reservation 记录从 reservations 里删除
why: 先让 inventory 反映真实扣减，再释放 reserved 里的占用，最后清掉已履行的记录，保证两个字段都对上。
why_en: Inventory is debited first, then the matching reserved count is freed, then the fulfilled record is removed, keeping both fields consistent.

scenario: releaseReservation 只对 reserved[productId] 做减法，从不碰 inventory[productId]。
scenario_en: releaseReservation only decrements reserved[productId] and never touches inventory[productId].
q: 为什么 release 不需要改动 inventory？
q_en: Why doesn't release need to touch inventory at all?
options: reserveStock 没减过 inventory，release 把 reserved 减回去就够
inventory 在 reserveStock 阶段已被扣减，release 需要把这部分补回来
release 需要把 inventory 和 reserved 都清零，避免统计出错
inventory 由后台任务定期重算，release 不必关心它
options_en: reserveStock never touched inventory, so release just needs to undo the reserved increment.
inventory was already debited during reserveStock, and release needs to restore that amount.
release should zero out both inventory and reserved to avoid bad counts.
inventory is recomputed periodically by a background job, so release doesn't need to touch it.
optionExplanations: 占用阶段只挪动了一个计数器，物理库存表从头到尾都没被写过一次。
把 reserve 和 confirm 搞反了：真正扣减 inventory 的是 confirmReservation，不是 reserveStock。
清零会凭空销毁真实库存，release 只是取消一次占用，不该动物理数量。
inventory 是被 add/removeStock 直接写入的权威数据，不是派生出来的定期重算值。
optionExplanations_en: The hold step only moves a counter; the physical stock table is never written the whole time.
This swaps reserve and confirm — inventory is actually debited by confirmReservation, not reserveStock.
Zeroing would destroy real stock out of nowhere; release only cancels one hold, not the physical count.
inventory is authoritative data written directly by add/removeStock, not a derived value recomputed on a schedule.
why: reserveStock 只增加 reserved 计数、不碰物理库存，所以 release 撤销占用时只需把 reserved 减回去。
why_en: reserveStock only bumps the reserved count and never touches physical inventory, so releasing a hold just undoes that reserved increment.

scenario: Warehouse 每次操作的临界区只是几次 map 读写，量级在几微秒；每秒几百次操作。
scenario_en: Each Warehouse operation's critical section is a couple of map lookups, on the order of microseconds, at a few hundred ops per second.
q: 这个量级下，粗粒度 warehouse 锁真的会成为瓶颈吗？
q_en: At this scale, does the coarse warehouse lock actually become a bottleneck?
options: 不会：几百次×几微秒远小于 1 秒，混入慢 I/O 才会真变瓶颈
会：任何加了锁的临界区，不管多快，锁本身就是瓶颈
不会：synchronized 关键字在任何负载下都是零开销
会：几百次操作已经超过单核每秒能完成的锁获取上限
options_en: No: hundreds of ops × microseconds is far under a second; slow I/O inside the lock is the real risk.
Yes: any locked critical section is a bottleneck no matter how fast it runs.
No: the synchronized keyword has zero overhead at any load.
Yes: a few hundred operations already exceed what one core can lock-acquire per second.
optionExplanations: 几百次×几微秒总占用远不到 1 秒，争用概率很低；真正拖成瓶颈的是锁内混入网络调用这类慢操作。
锁开销很小，是否成瓶颈取决于临界区时长和调用频率，不是有锁就是瓶颈。
synchronized 有获取释放的固定开销，只是在这个量级下小到可忽略，不是零开销。
现代 CPU 每秒可完成的锁获取是百万级，几百次离这个上限还差好几个数量级。
optionExplanations_en: Hundreds × microseconds totals far under a second, so contention stays low; slow work like network calls inside the lock is what actually creates a bottleneck.
Lock overhead is tiny; whether it bottlenecks depends on hold time and call rate, not merely the presence of a lock.
synchronized has real acquire/release overhead, just small enough to ignore at this scale — not zero.
Modern CPUs handle millions of lock acquisitions per second, orders of magnitude above a few hundred.
why: 公式：锁争用≈操作频率×临界区时长，几百次/秒×几微秒≈毫秒级总占用，远低于 1 秒；这个数字说明现在不必上 per-product 锁。
why_en: Formula: contention ≈ op rate × critical-section duration, hundreds/sec × microseconds ≈ single-digit milliseconds — well under a second, telling you per-product locking isn't needed yet.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持锁执行的那段代码，同一时刻只能被一个线程执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A critical section is code that runs while holding a lock, executable by only one thread at a time.

tradeoff: 现在就上 per-product 锁的复杂度 vs 当前争用低、粗粒度锁已经够用

scenario: 同一产品配置了两条告警：20 件预警、5 件紧急；库存从 25 一次跌到 3。
scenario_en: One product has two alert configs — a warning at 20 and an urgent alert at 5 — and stock drops from 25 straight to 3.
q: getAlertsToFire 这次该收集几条告警？
q_en: How many alerts should getAlertsToFire collect for this drop?
options: 两条都收集：25→3 同时跨过 20 和 5 这两条线
只收集 5 件那条：只有最接近当前库存的阈值才算穿越
只收集 20 件那条：先穿越的阈值优先，后面直接跳过
一条都不收集：库存变化要逐次相邻发生才算穿越
options_en: Both: the drop from 25 to 3 crosses both the 20 and 5 line.
